title: Order Entry Rules: Requisition Validity and Standing Orders by Service Class
content:
A physician requisition for Laboratory Test Orders has a validity period counted from its order date, and some service classes accept a standing (recurring) requisition.

| Service class | Requisition valid (calendar days from order date) | Standing requisition accepted | Standing requisition valid (calendar months from order date) | Maximum collections under one standing requisition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Routine Clinical Testing | 180 | Yes | 12 | 24 |
| Specialty Clinical Testing | 180 | Yes | 12 | 12 |
| Esoteric Reference Testing | 90 | No | 0 | 0 |
| Molecular Infectious Disease Testing | 30 | No | 0 | 0 |
| Clinical Toxicology Testing | 90 | Yes | 12 | 12 |
| Anatomic Pathology & Cytology | 30 | No | 0 | 0 |
| Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing | 90 | No | 0 | 0 |

## Terms

- **Requisition valid** — the calendar days from the order date within which a physician requisition must be collected before it expires.
- **Standing requisition accepted** — whether a recurring requisition is accepted for the class at all.
- **Standing requisition valid** — the calendar months a standing requisition stays valid from its order date; 0 where standing requisitions are not accepted.
- **Maximum collections** — the most collections one standing requisition may cover; 0 where not accepted.

## Comparison

Only three classes accept standing requisitions — Routine Clinical Testing, Specialty Clinical Testing and Clinical Toxicology Testing — each valid for 12 months; Routine allows up to 24 collections and the other two up to 12. Requisitions expire soonest in Molecular Infectious Disease Testing and Anatomic Pathology & Cytology (30 days) and latest in Routine and Specialty Clinical Testing (180 days).
